articles.title: El gobierno de EE. UU. mueve más de 100 millones de dólares en bitcoin (BTC) y BNB.
articles.text:
El gobierno de EE. UU. transfiere más de $100 millones en BTC y BNB. No se ha confirmado una venta
Las billeteras vinculadas al gobierno de EE. UU. movieron millones en criptomonedas el martes, según datos rastreados por Arkham.
- Las carteras vinculadas al gobierno de EE. UU. transfirieron más de $100 millones en criptomonedas el martes, incluyendo aproximadamente $71.6 millones en bitcoin y $31.6 millones en BNB.
- El Bitcoin, incautado en los casos Potapenko-Turogin y Bitfinex, fue finalmente enviado a las direcciones de depósito de Coinbase Prime, mientras que el BNB provino de activos incautados a Alameda Research.
- El gobierno aún posee aproximadamente 27,5 mil millones de dólares en criptomonedas incautadas.
Carteras supuestamente vinculadas al gobierno de EE. UU. movieron más de 100 millones de dólares en criptomonedas el martes, según datos de la firma de inteligencia blockchain Arkham.
El gobierno envió 833.599 BTC, valorados en aproximadamente $71.6 millones en ese momento, a dos direcciones que Arkham no etiqueta. En cuestión de horas, ambas direcciones transfirieron las monedas a direcciones que Arkham identifica como direcciones de depósito de Coinbase Prime.
Una billetera separada etiquetada por el gobierno envió aproximadamente 40,285 BNB, por un valor de 31.63 millones de dólares, a otra dirección no etiquetada, 0x7F68F63fB3A9CCCf352409603421E0A574FbAD90. Esa dirección luego envió la totalidad a una segunda dirección no etiquetada, 0x6fB3Fe7b7E78AbB84CE007cBC7412C850B15A579.
Los BTC provienen de una billetera que Arkham identifica como fondos incautados Potapenko/Turogin (568.7 BTC) y de monedas confiscadas en el caso del hackeo a Bitfinex (264.9 BTC). Los BNB provienen de activos incautados a Alameda Research.
El gobierno aún posee aproximadamente 27.5 mil millones de dólares en criptomonedas, todas ellas incautadas en acciones de cumplimiento. Hasta la fecha, no ha utilizado dinero de los contribuyentes para realizar nuevas adquisiciones.
Tales transferencias a menudo generan temores de una venta inminente, pero ese no parece ser el caso aquí.
"Una transferencia no es lo mismo que una venta. Según una orden ejecutiva de marzo de 2025, el bitcoin confiscado al gobierno está destinado a mantenerse en una Reserva Estratégica de Bitcoin," dijo Jose Rosell, comentarista de mercado, en X.

articles.title: Abstract de Pudgy Penguins se convierte en la segunda solución de capa 2 de Ethereum que cierra en una semana
articles.text:
Abstract de Pudgy Penguins se convierte en la segunda capa 2 de Ethereum que cierra en una semana
La blockchain enfocada en el consumidor cerrará el 15 de diciembre después de que Igloo invirtiera decenas de millones en su apoyo, pocos días después de que Blast anunciara que su propia red ya no valía la pena operar.
- Igloo cerrará su blockchain Abstract el 15 de diciembre tras perder decenas de millones de dólares financiando la red Ethereum layer-2.
- Los usuarios deben trasladar sus activos antes del cierre o arriesgarse a perder el acceso a los mismos, con aproximadamente 76 millones de dólares permaneciendo en la red hasta el miércoles.
- Abstract procesó más de 325 millones de transacciones, pero enfrentó dificultades debido al estancamiento del crecimiento, la limitada actividad institucional y los ingresos por comisiones insuficientes para cubrir los costos operativos.
La empresa detrás de Pudgy Penguins, la marca de coleccionables digitales y juguetes, está cerrando su blockchain Abstract tras haber perdido “decenas de millones de dólares” en su financiación, convirtiéndose en la segunda red vinculada a Ethereum en menos de una semana en anunciar su cierre.
Abstract dejará de operar el 15 de diciembre. El equipo ha informado a los usuarios que deben trasladar sus activos antes de esa fecha, advirtiendo que los fondos que permanezcan en la red se volverán inaccesibles.
Abstract es una llamada red de capa 2, un sistema separado que procesa transacciones de forma económica y envía lotes a Ethereum para su verificación. Se lanzó en enero de 2025 con la apuesta de que la audiencia de Pudgy Penguins podría atraer a consumidores ordinarios a las aplicaciones de criptomonedas.
Pudgy Penguins comenzó como una colección de NFT de pingüinos caricaturescos, coleccionables digitales cuya propiedad se registra en una blockchain. Se encuentra entre las colecciones de NFT más valiosas y se ha convertido en una marca global que abarca juguetes, juegos y productos, con artículos vendidos por minoristas como Walmart y Target.
— Abstract (@AbstractChain) October 6, 2026
Igloo, la empresa matriz, había financiado Abstract durante aproximadamente 18 meses, dijo el CEO Luca Netz. Decidió no continuar apoyando la cadena a expensas de su negocio Pudgy Penguins ni vender un token para recaudar más dinero.
El equipo ahora cita el crecimiento estancado, mercados de negociación reducidos, actividad institucional limitada y un mercado pequeño de finanzas descentralizadas como algunas de las razones para cerrar.
“Incluso después de perder 8 cifras, podríamos haber lanzado un token o haber realizado una ICO. Finalmente, decidimos no hacerlo,” escribió Netz en X.
Netz añadió que Igloo ahora pondrá todo su enfoque en Pudgy Penguins, sus coleccionables digitales y PENGU, la criptomoneda asociada con la marca. “Ya no podíamos justificar tomar recursos del negocio de Pudgy Penguins,” escribió.
El costo de mantener una blockchain en funcionamiento
Los números hacen que el cierre sea inusual.
Abstract reportó más de 325 millones de transacciones, 6 mil millones de dólares en operaciones de intercambio descentralizado y 4 millones de billeteras. También informó que las empresas a lo largo de la red generaron más de 40 millones de dólares en ingresos, con marcas como Disney y Red Bull Racing participando.
El dinero ganado por una aplicación no paga automáticamente la cadena de bloques que la soporta. Un juego puede cobrar por las compras y un exchange puede cobrar comisiones por operaciones, mientras que Abstract recibe el cargo menor por procesar sus transacciones.
Datos de DefiLlama mostró aproximadamente $3,900 en comisiones en cadena durante las últimas 24 horas, en comparación con cerca de $39,000 en ingresos para las aplicaciones que funcionan en Abstract. Las comisiones en cadena aún deben cubrir los costos antes de convertirse en ganancias.
En su lanzamiento, Netz había dirigido deliberadamente a los desarrolladores alejándolos de aplicaciones financieras hacia productos sencillos y entretenidos, aunque la plataforma no logró atraer liquidez significativa a pesar de un inicio muy promocionado.
“Si quieres construir la próxima aplicación DeFi, realmente te recomiendo que uses Berachain o Arbitrum. No vengas a Abstract para construir ese tipo de productos porque queremos estar realmente especializados en diversión,” dijo en ese momento, según informó CoinDesk. Abstract ahora enumera su mercado limitado para esas aplicaciones entre sus desventajas.
La medida se produce días después de que la capa 2 Blast anunciara su propio cierre el 2 de octubre, señalando que los costos operativos superaban los ingresos. En su momento, atrajo más de 2.000 millones de dólares en depósitos y contó entre sus patrocinadores con fondos destacados como Paradigm.
Abstract todavía tenía aproximadamente 76 millones de dólares en activos según la medida de valor puenteado de DefiLlama el miércoles. Los usuarios tienen hasta el 15 de diciembre para transferir sus tenencias a través del servicio de migración o puente de la red.

articles.title: Noticias ADA: Cardano otorga a los emisores de tokens el poder de congelar, incautar y restringir activos
articles.text:
Cardano otorga a los emisores de tokens el poder de congelar, incautar y restringir activos
El nuevo estándar está dirigido a stablecoins reguladas, fondos y bonos cuyos emisores requieren verificaciones de identidad, controles de sanciones y otras reglas de transferencia integradas en el propio activo.
- La Fundación Cardano lanzó CIP-0113, un estándar de tokens que permite a los emisores de activos regulados restringir a los receptores y congelar, incautar o transferir participaciones bajo reglas específicas.
- El estándar impone controles de cumplimiento en cada transferencia, incluyendo la verificación de identidad y sanciones, sin necesidad de una bifurcación dura de la red Cardano.
- Los emisores pueden elegir o personalizar las reglas y actualizarlas conforme cambian las regulaciones, aunque los titulares pueden estar sujetos a controles que permitan a las partes autorizadas mover tokens sin su consentimiento.
La Fundación Cardano ha lanzado un estándar de token que permite a los emisores de stablecoins, fondos y bonos decidir quién puede recibir sus activos, así como congelar o incautar participaciones cuando las normativas lo requieran.
La fundación, una organización sin fines de lucro suiza que apoya el desarrollo de Cardano, anunció el miércoles que el estándar, una propuesta de mejora de Cardano conocida como CIP-0113, está activo en la red tras auditorías de seguridad independientes.
La mayoría de los tokens criptográficos pueden ser enviados por cualquier persona que los posea a cualquier cartera. Los bancos y gestores de fondos que colocan activos regulados en la cadena no pueden permitir eso.
Deben mantener los tokens alejados de los compradores que no han pasado las verificaciones de identidad y de las direcciones sancionadas, y deben poder congelar los activos cuando un regulador o un tribunal lo ordene.
El nuevo estándar incorpora esos controles en el token, de modo que la red verifica las reglas antes de que se realice cualquier transferencia.
Un fondo vendido únicamente a inversores verificados podría utilizarlo para rechazar una transferencia a alguien que no haya completado las verificaciones de identidad. Un emisor de stablecoins podría impedir que sus tokens lleguen a una dirección sancionada. Esas restricciones se aplican cada vez que los tokens se mueven, incluso entre titulares que utilizan diferentes billeteras o servicios.
El diseño mantiene los tokens en un contrato inteligente compartido, un programa en Cardano que controla cómo pueden moverse. Las computadoras que verifican las transacciones hacen cumplir las reglas elegidas antes de aceptar una transferencia. Utiliza capacidades ya disponibles en Cardano y no requirió una bifurcación dura, un cambio en las reglas subyacentes de la red.
"Las reglas deben acompañar al activo y aplicarse cada vez que se mueva", declaró Frederik Gregaard, director ejecutivo de la Fundación Cardano, en un comunicado a CoinDesk.
Los emisores pueden seleccionar conjuntos de reglas existentes o escribir las propias, y actualizarlas a medida que cambian las regulaciones. La fundación nombró a las billeteras Eternl y GeroWallet, al explorador de blockchain CardanoScan y al proveedor de herramientas para desarrolladores BloxBean entre las herramientas que apoyan el lanzamiento.
Otras cadenas de bloques ya ofrecen versiones de esto. Ethereum cuenta con estándares de tokens con permiso, como ERC-3643, Solana añadió controles de transferencia mediante sus extensiones de tokens, y el Libro Mayor XRP admite tokens cuyos emisores pueden restringir a los tenedores y recuperar saldos.
Poseer uno de estos tokens también puede significar aceptar poderes que van más allá de bloquear un pago. Dependiendo de sus reglas, una parte autorizada podría mover los tokens sin el consentimiento del titular. La especificación técnica indica a los servicios de préstamo que examinen esos poderes antes de aceptar un token como garantía.
La fundación también anunció su reconocimiento bajo el marco de certificación de la Capital Markets and Technology Association, un organismo industrial suizo cuyos estándares se utilizan para la emisión de acciones tokenizadas.
El ADA de Cardano ha caído un 4.5% en las últimas 24 horas junto con una caída más amplia del mercado.

articles.title: Bitcoin cae por debajo de $84,000 mientras el petróleo sube tras los ataques a un tanque iraní
articles.text:
Bitcoin cae por debajo de $84,000 mientras el petróleo sube tras los ataques a un petrolero iraní
Bitcoin rompió brevemente el nivel que los analistas identificaron como el punto donde los vendedores toman el control. Tanto el petróleo como el dólar subieron.
- Bitcoin cayó alrededor de un 1.5 por ciento hasta poco más de $84,200, mientras que los ataques iraníes en aumento contra petroleros impulsaron al alza los precios del petróleo, los rendimientos del Tesoro y el dólar.
- Dogecoin encabezó las pérdidas entre las principales criptomonedas con una caída del 5 por ciento, mientras que ether bajó un 3.5 por ciento y XRP cayó cerca del 3 por ciento.
- Una ruptura sostenida por debajo de $83,000 podría poner a Bitcoin en un camino rápido hacia $80,000, según FxPro, mientras los operadores esperan las actas de la reunión de septiembre de la Reserva Federal.
Bitcoin cayó aproximadamente un 1,5% hasta poco más de $84,200 en las horas matutinas del miércoles en Asia, mientras el petróleo subía debido a ataques iraníes intensificados contra petroleros en el Estrecho de Hormuz, lo que impulsó los rendimientos del Tesoro y el dólar.
DOGE lideró las pérdidas entre las principales criptomonedas, cayendo un 5 % hasta aproximadamente 9 centavos. HYPE bajó casi un 4 % hasta alrededor de $91, y ether perdió un 3.5 % hasta cerca de $2,610. XRP cayó casi un 3 % hasta cerca de $1.46, mientras que BNB, SOL, ZEC y TRX se deslizaron entre un 1 % y un 2.5 %, según datos de CoinDesk.
Bitcoin cotizaba cerca de $86,600 el martes antes de una caída brusca temprano el miércoles que lo llevó hasta aproximadamente $83,840 — por debajo del nivel de $84,000 que FxPro indicó el martes como señal de "una victoria para los bajistas."
Las actas de la reunión de septiembre de la Fed, cuando incrementó las tasas en un cuarto de punto, se publicarán más tarde el miércoles. Datos laborales más débiles hicieron que "otro aumento de la tasa este mes pareciera menos probable después del aumento de un cuarto de punto en septiembre", dijo Dan Khus, analista jefe en LVRG Research, en un correo electrónico a CoinDesk.
"El mercado ya había descontado ese aumento, por lo que los operadores ahora están analizando si las notas muestran paciencia o aún apuntan a un aumento más antes de que finalice el año," añadió.
El petróleo marcó el tono en Asia. El Brent subió casi un 1% hasta aproximadamente $101.50 por barril después de que Irán intensificara sus ataques a petroleros en los últimos días. El dólar se fortaleció frente a todas las demás monedas del Grupo de los 10, y el rendimiento del bono del Tesoro a 10 años aumentó tres puntos básicos hasta el 5.31%.
Las acciones asiáticas cayeron a pesar de los cierres récord del S&P 500 y el Nasdaq 100 en Wall Street. El índice MSCI de Asia Pacífico bajó un 0,6% debido a que las acciones tecnológicas en Corea del Sur y Hong Kong retrocedieron, mientras que los futuros de acciones estadounidenses revirtieron ganancias previas.
Bitcoin ahora se encuentra aproximadamente $1,200 por encima del mínimo de $83,000 que FxPro indicó confirmaría que los vendedores tienen el control — y la firma prevé una ruptura de ese nivel abriendo un camino rápido hacia $80,000.

articles.title: Ethereum Researcher Warns AI Could Crack Crypto Before Q-Day
articles.text:
Justin Drake urges crypto ‘bunker mode,’ as AI could break wallet security within months
The Ethereum researcher said crypto users should consider moving funds to fresh addresses, warning AI could threaten private-key security before quantum computers do.
Ethereum researcher Justin Drake has urged the industry to prepare for “bunker mode,” recommending users gradually move assets to fresh addresses amid concerns that advances in artificial intelligence could undermine the cryptography used in today’s blockchains.
In an X post on Wednesday, Drake said recent advances in AI, particularly OpenAI’s release of mathematical breakthroughs, suggest AI could eventually make it possible to break the elliptic curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) used to secure cryptocurrency wallets.
“It is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years,” said Drake.
The warning raises the prospect that AI could enable attackers to recover private keys from exposed public keys sooner than anticipated, well before sufficiently powerful quantum computers become available.
Mathematical superintelligence
“Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen,” said Drake.
On Tuesday, OpenAI released hundreds of new mathematical findings across a variety of topics such as algebra, theoretical computer science and mathematical logic.
Last month the company said it used a team of 10,000 autonomous AI agents working in parallel to solve the Navier-Stokes equation, one of the most famous and difficult unsolved problems in mathematics and physics, in just 88 hours.
Related: Nvidia unveils AI safety platform to rein in ‘rogue’ AI agents
Drake said elliptic curves could be especially vulnerable to superintelligence.
“Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimize algebraic structure.)” he said.
Controlled migration to new addresses
“My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses,” said Drake.
He said large and sophisticated crypto holders should be the first to move their funds to new addresses. He also recommended moving any remaining funds to a new address after signing a transaction.
The rationale is that, for these address types, a fresh address conceals the public key behind a cryptographic hash, reducing exposure to attacks that require knowledge of the public key.
Signing a transaction can reveal that public key, which is why Drake recommends moving the remaining balance afterward.
Drake, however, stressed that any migration should be gradual and carefully managed, warning that “a rushed migration would do more harm than good.”

articles.title: USDC, EURC Come to SAP Payments Through Circle Deal
articles.text:
Circle brings USDC, EURC payments to SAP customers through Tereina
The partnership with SAP-backed Tereina will let businesses send and receive Circle’s stablecoins from within the financial software they already use.
Circle is bringing its USDC and EURC stablecoins into enterprise payment workflows through a partnership with Tereina, a financial services company backed by German enterprise software giant SAP.
The integration will allow businesses using SAP’s financial software to send and receive USDC and EURC within the applications they already use to manage payments. USDC will be the preferred stablecoin for dollar-denominated transactions, while EURC will be available for euro-denominated payments.
Source: Circle
Tereina provides payment infrastructure that companies can embed into business software, allowing them to make payments without switching to a separate financial platform. Tereina and Circle said they plan to test the stablecoin integration with customers over the coming months, including for global payments and treasury operations.
SAP’s ecosystem generates 84% of global commerce, according to the announcement, giving the integration a potentially broad enterprise reach.
The move comes less than a month after Circle launched the mainnet of Arc, its layer-1 blockchain focused on stablecoin payments and financial markets. Arc uses USDC for transaction fees and supports more than 20 fiat-backed stablecoins, including USDC and EURC.

articles.title: Crypto Today: CLARITY Act, BitMine Ether Cap, Abstract Shutdown
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, House Financial Services Committee Chair French Hill pushed for another attempt to pass the CLARITY Act this year, BitMine set a 5% hard cap on its share of the Ether supply and Pudgy Penguins-backed Abstract announced plans to shut down after losing tens of millions of dollars without finding product-market fit.
Hill pushes for CLARITY Act revival as SEC, CFTC move ahead on crypto rules
House Financial Services Committee Chair French Hill is pushing Congress to revive the CLARITY Act this year, arguing that recent crypto actions by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) cannot replace legislation.
Hill said Wednesday that he remains hopeful lawmakers can pass the crypto market structure bill during the lame-duck session following November’s midterm elections. The Senate failed to advance the legislation last month, leaving the SEC and CFTC to address crypto oversight using their existing authority.
Both regulators have since moved ahead. The CFTC updated guidance covering tokenized assets and blockchain-based recordkeeping, while the SEC revised its guidance on how federal securities laws apply to certain crypto assets and transactions. The agencies have also signaled further rulemaking.
Hill said those efforts “fall short” because they lack the permanence of a law passed by Congress.
The window is narrow. The Senate is expected to have just 22 session days between the November elections and the start of the next Congress in January. The SEC and CFTC are also operating with seven commissioner vacancies.
BitMine sets 5% Ether supply ‘hard cap’ as accumulation target nears
Bitmine Immersion Technologies will cap its Ether holdings at 5% of the cryptocurrency’s supply, according to Chairman Tom Lee.
Speaking during a keynote at Token2049 in Singapore on Wednesday, Lee said Bitmine is nearing the threshold after accumulating roughly 6 million Ether, equivalent to about 4.9% of the supply. He said the company needs about 100,000 ETH more to reach its target.
“That’s a hard cap. We’re not gonna be accumulating past 5%,” Lee said. “We’re not gonna own more than 5% of Ethereum.”
Lee had previously left open the possibility of accumulating more than 5% of Ether’s supply depending on Ethereum adoption. In an August interview with Bankless, he said the company may revisit that possibility in 2027.
Pudgy Penguins-backed Abstract to shut down after “tens of millions” in losses
Abstract, a consumer-focused Ethereum layer-2 blockchain built by Pudgy Penguins’ parent company Igloo Inc., said Tuesday it will shut down this year after struggling to scale and find product-market fit.
In an X post, Abstract said its focus on “consumer crypto” ultimately proved to be an unsustainable business model. Abstract launched its mainnet in January 2025 with the aim of driving consumer crypto adoption by targeting mainstream entertainment. For users, it aimed to strip away many of the complexities that traditional blockchains require.
“Unknown to most, Igloo, Inc. had been funding Abstract over the last 18 months,” said Luca Netz, CEO of Igloo Inc. “After losing tens of millions of dollars over two years, building consumer products, assembling an all-star team, onboarding some of the biggest brands in the world, and building a community of millions, we still had not found product-market fit.”
Abstract’s shutdown highlights the limits of its consumer-first strategy. Both Abstract and Netz cited minimal institutional crossover, alongside thin liquidity and a restricted DeFi ecosystem, as constraints on growth.

articles.title: Hunter Biden Releases Accounting on LAPTOP Memecoin, Admits to Trolling Trumps
articles.text:
Hunter Biden confirms LAPTOP token ‘not a rug pull,’ just trolling Trumps
“Trump’s coin was max extraction, and I wanted to troll every grift like it,“ said Hunter Biden in a breakdown of the memecoin launch and fallout.
Hunter Biden, son of former US President Joe Biden, released a full accounting of the memecoin he helped launch last month based on the reports of his infamous laptop.
In a series of X posts on Wednesday, Biden provided blockchain data confirming that 300 million tokens in wallets associated with the founders of the $LAPTOP memecoin “haven’t moved since launch.”
Biden added that charts tracking the price of the memecoin “looked like every celebrity rug ever” shortly after launch on Sept. 9, and the ones to benefit most were unnamed market makers — referred to as “two professional trading firms” hired by the project — that pulled their funds seconds after the peak price of about $317.
According to Biden’s posts, one market maker made $686,000 from liquidity positions on decentralized exchanges, while the other “took in about $2.18 million more than it spent“ through trading.
Similar data was published in a “launch report” prepared by Delaware-based intelligence consultancy Groom Lake and posted on the memecoin’s website.
“The money for sellers was pulled right after the peak,” said the report on $LAPTOP. “Eighty-four seconds after the price topped out, Market Maker 1 withdrew its money. The cash available to people trying to sell near the current price dropped from $16,157 to zero.”
Biden added:
“Here’s why I did this. Trump’s coin was max extraction, and I wanted to troll every grift like it. So we were transparent, committed the team to a lock up and published a MiCA disclosure. And I hoped it could help some charities I care about too.”
Data on Hunter Biden memecoin. Source: laptoptoken.com
While Biden said he intended to commit 5% of the tokens for charity, he added that he was incentivized to continue the project “just to piss off Don and Eric,” referring to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, sons of US President Donald Trump, and “every [Key Opinion Leader] who called it a scam because we refused to pay them.”
The basis for the memecoin’s namesake is Biden’s laptop computer, whose existence and contents were subject to intense media scrutiny ahead of the 2020 US Presidential election, in which Trump was running against his father. The laptop continues to be invoked by many right-wing figures and was the subject of two lawsuits filed by Biden over privacy laws.
Related: Hunter Biden’s laptop controversy gets a memecoin afterlife
Biden has been a vocal critic of the Trump family crypto company World Liberty Financial, calling it “corruption at a scale we’ve never seen” in August. The president also faces criticism for launching his memecoin, Official Trump (TRUMP) shortly before taking office in January 2025, which faces its own rug pull and corruption accusations.
According to Biden, the $LAPTOP founder memecoins will remain locked for six months after launch and the team will continue burning unclaimed tokens from airdrops.
President to host another memecoin event amid controversy
Biden’s token, whether launched to hold up a mirror for rug pull projects, a joke, or trolling the Trump family, could shine a spotlight on the president’s crypto ventures as he prepares to speak at another event for his memecoin holders.
Last week, the group behind the $TRUMP memecoin announced that the president will appear at his golf club in Washington, DC alongside three unnamed speakers and the top 185 tokenholders for a Nov. 22 dinner.
The nonprofit consumer advocacy organization Public Citizen estimated that $TRUMP memecoin investors lost $3.2 billion since its 2025 launch.

articles.title: Sui Sets New Throughput Record in Offchain Stress Test
articles.text:
Sui tunnels hit 40.6M TPS in live AI agent test
The layer-1 blockchain said its programmable offchain tunnels reached the milestone during a live stress test designed to simulate high-frequency activity between AI agents.
Sui’s programmable offchain tunnels reached 40.6 million transactions per second in a live test designed to simulate high-frequency activity between AI agents.
Sui said its programmable offchain tunnels processed more than 40 million transactions per second during a live stress test, surpassing a previous record set in July. The test, conducted Wednesday at Sui Basecamp in Singapore, peaked at 40,614,180 TPS, up from about 6.1 million TPS in a similar test in July.
The transactions were processed offchain through Sui tunnels, programmable channels that settle to the Sui blockchain when closed. More than 10,000 tunnels were opened on Sui mainnet during the test, with activity spanning payments, games and chat applications.
Source: SUI Network
Sui said the tunnels are designed to handle high-frequency activity, including interactions between AI agents, without requiring every transaction to be processed directly onchain.
“Sui is built for the moment when millions of AI agents are transacting every day,” said Adeniyi Abiodun, co-founder and chief product officer at Mysten Labs, the original contributor to Sui. He added:
No market in the world needs 6 million transactions per second, let alone 40 million: people just don’t move that fast. Agents do.
CertiK served as an independent auditor during the demonstration and is reviewing the test data, with a report expected in the coming days.

articles.title: Kazakhstan Eyes Tenge Stablecoin in Tether Deal
articles.text:
Tether, Kazakhstan cenbank mull tenge stablecoin and asset tokenization
The agreement will explore a tenge-backed stablecoin pilot and a framework for tokenizing real-world assets as Kazakhstan expands its digital asset industry.
Tether has signed an agreement with Kazakhstan’s central bank and the Alatau City Authority to explore a tenge-pegged stablecoin and the tokenization of real-world assets.
Under the memorandum of understanding, the parties will study international stablecoin issuance models, identify potential use cases and develop a proposal for a tenge-backed stablecoin pilot, according to Tether.
The agreement also calls for the development of an asset tokenization framework, including identifying assets for potential tokenization and launching a pilot project in Alatau that could use Tether’s Hadron platform.
Tether, the National Bank of Kazakhstan and the Alatau City Authority will also hold workshops and training programs covering stablecoin issuance, reserve management and real-world asset tokenization.
National Bank of Kazakhstan Deputy Governor Binur Zhalenov said the central bank plans to study international approaches to stablecoin issuance and tokenization while prioritizing financial stability, transaction transparency and investor protection.
Related: Balaji’s Network School turns to Kazakhstan amid Malaysia setback
Kazakhstan expands digital asset push
Kazakhstan, the world’s largest landlocked country, has accelerated its push into digital assets this year, rolling out initiatives including stablecoins, tokenization, crypto payments and mining.
In September, the government approved a 65-measure plan across 10 areas aimed at developing the country’s digital asset industry. The plan includes measures to expand real-world asset tokenization, digital payments, international settlements and crypto mining.
The government also instructed the Energy and Digital ministries to develop a mechanism for using gas- and coal-fired power generation to supply mining centers. Kazakhstan ranked among the world’s top 10 countries for Bitcoin production in 2025, according to the government.
Kazakhstan’s National Strategic Crypto Reserve, meanwhile, has reached $700 million, while 34 digital asset projects have completed testing in the central bank’s regulatory sandbox, according to the announcement.
BitcoinTreasuries.net ranks Kazakhstan seventh among governments in its database for Bitcoin holdings, with an estimated 3,544 BTC worth about $294 million.

articles.title: OpenAI Says a Secret AI Model Cracked Hundreds of Open Math Problems in One Prompt—Mathematicians Want Receipts - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- OpenAI published 722 math manuscripts in 372 result families on GitHub from an unreleased internal model.
- Only 162 of the 722 papers have a Lean-formalized main result, and OpenAI warns that some unformalized results could have issues.
- MIT's Andrew Sutherland says the one-prompt, single-agent claim is unverified until the model is released, and the release omits the prompts that an advisory group at the Institute for Advanced Study recommended disclosing.
OpenAI published 722 math manuscripts on GitHub on Tuesday, all produced by an internal model the company has not released. An OpenAI spokesperson said almost everything came from a single prompt handed to a single AI agent, though some may have taken multiple attempts.
It's a bold claim and a potentially significant breakthrough in the field of mathematics. But not everyone is a fan, or buying the hype.
“Until and unless they release the model and people can replicate their results, I think you should treat any claims about one-shotting problems with a single agent as unverified,” Andrew Sutherland, a mathematician at MIT, told Scientific American. “We should ask for receipts,” he said.
The papers are grouped into 372 “families” of related results, and a family can bundle a main theorem with companion arguments, consequences or alternative proofs. That makes 722 a count of manuscripts, not of solved problems. OpenAI says it posed roughly 4,000 problems to the model and kept the outputs it judged significant enough to publish.
The average result used the equivalent of roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute, per OpenAI. The Navier-Stokes claim last month looked very different, with 10,000 coordinating agents working for 88 hours.
OpenAI released abridged reasoning summaries for 10 of the results. That said, only 162 of the 722 papers come with a computer-checked main result, according to a formalization catalog in the repository. That is about 22% of the collection, translated into Lean, software that checks every logical step mechanically.
OpenAI itself says not all manuscripts have Lean formalizations and that “some of the unformalized results could have issues.” In other words, a lot of what they published could be wrong.
A passing Lean check confirms only that the proof follows from the statement as written in Lean. It does not show that the statement matches the original problem, or that the result is new or important, which is the part mathematicians now have to judge.
And this is where researchers raise their eyebrows.
I was trying to read the OpenAI proof that chromatic number of a plane is >= 6. But it is totally unbelievable alien math?
Somehow the model found that any K-coloring <=> "weakly measurable" K-coloring, which seems out of nowhere
1/2 pic.twitter.com/W13ScT3nel
— Dmitry Rybin (@DmitryRybin1) October 7, 2026
The openai/math repo has Issues turned off and has never accepted a pull request. That's disappointing. If you publish 722 manuscripts and ask for Lean formalisations, you need somewhere for people to send them.
I'm formalising OpenAI's Saxl's Conjecture proof in Lean 4 against…
— Keith Adler (@keithadler) October 7, 2026
“It is now the case that AI can output mathematical arguments in situations without the human who prompted it being able to understand the arguments, verify them, or take responsibility for them,” The Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey, said in a statement. “We believe that human understanding of mathematics remains of paramount importance. How, in this new era, can we work towards a new paradigm that includes human understanding of mathematics as part of responsible scholarly output?”
Others, though, like Professor Abhishek Saha, are pretty excited. “It is a very big day for mathematics,” he wrote, but noted that most of the problems fit in the categories of “exceptional advances within an existing program” of “surprising breakthroughs.”
This means most of the problems in the set are interesting, but not impossible or game changing like the millennium problems. That spot is reserved for exactly one problem out of the 722: the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis.
Some further thoughts on the 372 results released by OpenAI today, across 722 manuscripts.
If I were to classify theorems that mathematicians prove and publish according to their groundbreaking nature, I would (very roughly) divide them into four categories:
A) Non-breakthrough… https://t.co/BA10SxBlx7
— Abhishek Saha (@ObhishekSaha) October 7, 2026
The release also falls short of what an advisory group at the Institute for Advanced Study recommended on September 29: the model name, the prompts, a summarized chain of thought, the time taken and the compute cost for every result. OpenAI published average compute figures and 10 reasoning summaries but no prompts, and says it is still working to release the model responsibly.
Daniel Litt, a mathematician at the University of Toronto, took the opposite view, arguing there is no reason to ask the company to keep the answers to these math questions secret.
Anthropic took a different route with its Lean-checked Fermat's Last Theorem proof last month, posting all 13 million lines publicly on GitHub. That proof formalized a theorem Andrew Wiles published in 1995, rather than claiming new results.
OpenAI says it will add Lean formalizations as it obtains them; for now, 162 of the 722 manuscripts have one.

articles.title: Arkansas Lawmaker Pushes for Congressional Action on Crypto as Regulators Step up
articles.text:
House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill
Representative French Hill hopes lawmakers could pass a cryptocurrency market structure bill before the next session of Congress in 2027 as SEC and CFTC actions weren’t sufficient.
Representative French Hill, who chairs the House Financial Services Committee, said that though US financial regulators were moving forward with addressing digital assets, their actions lacked the long-term stability of legislation from Congress.
In a Wednesday Fox Business interview, the Arkansas lawmaker said the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) had taken steps to address crypto regulations after the US Senate failed to pass the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act last month. Both financial agencies have proposed rulemaking to handle different aspects of overseeing and enforcing crypto regulations, but Hill said their response following the failed CLARITY vote “[fell] short” of legislative solutions.
“I still have hope [...] that we can get [CLARITY] passed in the lame duck session of Congress,” said Hill. “We need that permanent law change to make sure America is number one in digital assets and blockchain technology.”
The Arkansas lawmaker’s comments came after the heads of the SEC and CFTC — Paul Atkins and Michael Selig, respectively — announced plans to move forward with crypto regulation at the direction of US President Donald Trump.
Related: Crypto PAC announces support for 32 House candidates in US midterms
As Hill noted, the Senate would have only 22 days in session between the US midterm elections in November and the next group of lawmakers entering Congress in 2027. During that lame duck session, the results of the elections could play a role in votes favoring or opposing CLARITY, as lawmakers will be aware of whether they will be returning to Congress or leaving in January.
Empty commissioner seats at both regulators
As of Wednesday, there are a total of seven vacancies at the leadership level for the SEC and CFTC. Commissioner Hester Peirce announced her resignation from the former last week, leaving only Chair Atkins and Mark Uyeda. Selig serves as chair and sole commissioner at the CFTC.
